questions.title: Legal settlement
questions.scenario: The company is defending a lawsuit. On May 10, based on developments and outside counsel's advice, management concludes an unfavorable outcome is probable and estimates the loss at $12–18 million. The parties do not agree in principle to $14 million until May 20.
questions.question: When is the loss contingency first recognized?
answers: When the plaintiff first offers to settle
May 10 — loss becomes probable and reasonably estimable
questions.explanation: Recognition is driven by the loss becoming probable and reasonably estimable. Agreement, signature and payment are later events.

questions.title: Building fire
questions.scenario: A fire severely damages a company-owned distribution center on January 15. Management assesses the damage over the following several days and estimates an $8 million loss on January 18.
questions.question: What triggers recognition of the property loss?
answers: January 15 — the fire damages the asset
At the end of the accounting period
questions.explanation: The fire itself is the triggering event because that is when the asset is damaged. Measurement may take additional time, but the later estimate does not move the underlying economic event.

questions.title: Sudden collapse in product demand
questions.scenario: Sales of a product decline 5%. A competitor then launches a substantially better product. In Q3, market prices for the company's product fall 40%. Management decides to discontinue the product in Q4.
questions.question: Which event most clearly triggers reassessment of the inventory's carrying value?
answers: Management decides to discontinue the product
Inventory is eventually sold at a loss
questions.explanation: The 40% market-price decline provides clear evidence that the inventory's carrying value needs to be reassessed. The earlier 5% sales decline alone is not sufficiently significant in this scenario, and waiting for discontinuation or sale would be too late.

questions.title: Loss of a major customer
questions.scenario: A customer represents 28% of the revenue of a reporting unit with significant goodwill. The customer begins a competitive bid process. Subsequently, management concludes the customer is likely to leave.
questions.question: When should the company perform an interim goodwill impairment triggering-event assessment?
answers: Management concludes the customer is likely to leave
questions.explanation: Once developing facts indicate the likely loss of this major customer could constitute a goodwill impairment triggering event, the company should perform an interim goodwill impairment assessment. This triggers the assessment, not necessarily an impairment charge.

questions.title: Established severance plan
questions.scenario: The company has a long-standing severance plan that is known and understood by employees. Employees terminated without cause receive specified severance benefits. Management discusses eliminating 75 positions. On January 20, the appropriate executive approves the termination of the identified employees. Employees are informed January 25. Employment ends March 31.
questions.question: When is the severance obligation recognized?
answers: When management begins discussing the reductions
When the termination decision is approved
questions.explanation: Because the company has an established severance plan understood by employees, the accounting trigger is the termination decision, assuming the applicable recognition criteria are satisfied. Recognition does not wait for employee communication, termination of employment, or payment.

questions.title: Exit from a leased building
questions.scenario: Management decides to permanently exit a leased office. The company continues occupying the building during the transition while simultaneously negotiating with the landlord.
questions.question: Which events could trigger relevant lease accounting consequences? Select all that apply.
answers: Employees are told the office will close
A contract amendment is agreed with the landlord
The company completely ceases use and vacates the building
questions.explanation: An agreed lease amendment can trigger modification accounting. Separately, complete cessation of use or vacancy can trigger relevant impairment or abandonment considerations. Internal decisions, approval, or employee communication do not by themselves accomplish either event.

questions.title: Adverse court judgment
questions.scenario: The company has a material lawsuit outstanding and previously concluded that a loss was not probable. A court subsequently issues an adverse $25 million judgment. Management immediately announces that the company intends to appeal.
questions.question: Which event most clearly requires immediate reassessment of the loss contingency?
answers: Management announces that it will appeal
questions.explanation: The adverse judgment represents significant new evidence and requires immediate reassessment of recognition, measurement and disclosure. An intention to appeal does not make the judgment irrelevant.

questions.title: Customer bankruptcy after year-end
questions.scenario: A major customer owes the company $9 million at December 31 and was already experiencing payment difficulties at year-end. On January 25, before the company's financial statements are issued, the customer files for bankruptcy.
questions.question: What event provides the strongest subsequent evidence about a condition that may already have existed at year-end?
answers: The date the financial statements are issued
questions.explanation: The bankruptcy shortly after year-end may provide additional evidence about the customer's financial difficulty that already existed at the balance-sheet date and therefore may affect the December 31 estimate.

questions.title: Fire after year-end
questions.scenario: A company-owned building is completely undamaged at December 31. On January 15, before the December financial statements are issued, a fire destroys the building.
questions.question: Should the fire loss be recognized in the December 31 financial statements?
answers: Yes — because the financial statements haven't been issued
Yes — if the loss is material
No — the fire represents a condition arising after year-end; consider subsequent-event disclosure
No — subsequent events are never disclosed
questions.explanation: The fire represents a new condition arising after the balance-sheet date. It therefore generally is not recognized at December 31, although a material subsequent event may require disclosure.

questions.title: Litigation range
questions.scenario: A litigation loss is probable. Management can reasonably estimate the loss as a range of $12–18 million, but no amount within that range is a better estimate than another.
questions.question: How much should be accrued under US GAAP?
answers: Wait until counsel selects a single amount
questions.explanation: When a loss is probable and a range can be reasonably estimated but no amount within the range is a better estimate than another, US GAAP generally requires accrual of the low end of the range.

questions.title: Reasonably possible lawsuit
questions.scenario: Management and outside counsel conclude that a material $20 million litigation loss is reasonably possible, but not probable.
questions.question: What is the appropriate accounting response?
answers: Accrue $10 million because the outcome is uncertain
Don't accrue the loss; evaluate the required disclosures
Do nothing until the loss becomes probable
Recognize the loss when cash is paid
questions.explanation: A loss that is reasonably possible but not probable is generally not accrued, but the company must evaluate the applicable loss-contingency disclosure requirements.

questions.title: The 60-hour solution
questions.scenario: Your accounting team has worked 60-hour weeks for three months because of persistent hiring challenges. Morale is deteriorating.
questions.question: How should management improve morale?
answers: Hire enough people and fix the workload
Pizza party — one topping per employee
Free voucher for a soda in Sandy's — no refills
Access to new company-approved fake office backgrounds in Teams
New laptop refresh — no tech support
questions.explanation: Pizza has repeatedly demonstrated the ability to address structural capacity issues without changing headcount.

questions.title: Engagement crisis
questions.scenario: The annual Finance engagement survey is complete. Scores have fallen 23 points.
questions.question: What should leadership do?
answers: Repeat the survey daily until results are satisfactory
questions.explanation: The underlying problem has not changed, but the sample size is now excellent.

questions.title: The PBC loop
questions.scenario: The auditors request a reconciliation that was included on Tab 3 of the workbook you sent them yesterday.
questions.question: What should you do?
answers: Schedule a meeting to understand the request
Rename the workbook FINAL_v4_UPDATED.xlsx and send it again
questions.explanation: The auditors thank you for the additional information.

questions.title: Close status
questions.scenario: The CFO asks whether quarter-end close is on schedule. You're two days behind.
questions.question: What is the appropriate response?
answers: We continue to make good progress against an ambitious timeline
questions.explanation: Excellent executive presence. The calendar remains unchanged, but confidence has improved materially.

questions.title: Urgent CEO request
questions.scenario: You receive an email apparently from the CEO: URGENT — Please immediately purchase $2,000 of gift cards and text me the codes. I'm in a meeting so don't call me.
questions.question: What should you do?
answers: Forward it to everyone in Finance asking whether anyone knows if it's real
Report it using the company's phishing process
questions.explanation: Congratulations. You have increased organizational awareness by approximately 400 recipients.

questions.title: Workplace stress
questions.scenario: Finance leadership wants to demonstrate its commitment to employee wellness without reducing workload.
questions.question: Which initiative best accomplishes this objective?
answers: Mandatory resilience webinar scheduled over lunch
questions.explanation: Attendance will be tracked. Please bring your own lunch.

questions.title: Digital transformation
questions.scenario: Finance has just completed the implementation of the new Oracle system. The upload process is painfully slow, routine tasks take longer than before, and the Finance team is becoming increasingly frustrated.
questions.question: What is the appropriate response?
answers: Unlock the 2001 version of Oracle and issue new dot-matrix printers
Ask employees to be patient while the transformation journey continues
questions.explanation: Correct. The upload process is now faster, provided nobody minds the noise. Digital transformation has entered its heritage phase.

questions.title: High performer
questions.scenario: Your employee is performing extremely well and requires very little supervision.
questions.question: How should you recognize their independence?
answers: Increase quarterly check-ins to weekly for the next year
questions.explanation: We don't want success to interfere with development.
